cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. We're still listening to the words of the wise, and the teacher talks to his listener like a dad. He calls him "My son," and he starts with what makes HIS heart happy.

cards.question: The teacher says his own heart will rejoice. What would do it?
The teacher says his inmost being will rejoice when his son's ___ speak what is right.

cards.text: Then a warning: don't let your heart envy sinners. I know, friend, some days the guy parked in the fire lane gets the best spot EVERY single time.

cards.question: Instead of envying sinners, what does the teacher tell his son to always continue in?

cards.text: And he says why it's worth sticking with: surely there is a future. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, trust me, that's a line you want somebody to say to you.

cards.question: The teacher tells his son that his hope will be cut off.

cards.text: "Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course." Then he points out a crowd his son should stay away from.

cards.question: The teacher tells his son not to join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat.
The teacher says the drunkard and the glutton will come to ___.

cards.text: And he adds, "drowsiness will clothe them in rags." Years lying around in a junk drawer, and my whole outfit was DUST, head to toe, designer dust.
Now the teacher brings it home: listen to your father who gave you life. Then he has a word about the son's mother too.

cards.question: What does the teacher tell the son about his mother?

answers.text: Do not despise her when she is old
Do not leave her when you marry
Do not argue with her at the gate

cards.text: Then he sounds like a financial advisor: invest in truth, he says, in wisdom and instruction and understanding. FINALLY, an investment I don't have to check every five minutes on my phone.

cards.question: The teacher says to invest in truth and never ___ it.

cards.text: Then the teacher comes back around to where he started: what a son like that means to his father.

cards.question: The teacher says the father of a righteous man will worry over him.

cards.text: Then he wishes the son's parents joy: "May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice!" Nobody gave ME birth, friend, but when Mother Miller found me in a 25-cent bin, she smiled like I was worth a million.
"My son, give me your heart," the teacher says, "and let your eyes delight in my ways." Then he warns his son about the prostitute and the adulteress.

cards.question: The teacher calls the prostitute a deep pit and the adulteress a narrow well.

cards.text: Then he adds one more picture: she lies in wait like a robber.

cards.question: Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the ___ among men.

cards.text: Then the teacher fires off questions like a game show host: "Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?" Six questions with no commercial break, and I'm out of breath just READING it.

cards.question: The teacher says woe, sorrow and bloodshot eyes belong to those who linger over ___.

cards.text: Then he describes wine looking its very best. Red, sparkling in the cup, going down smoothly.

cards.question: The teacher tells his son to gaze at the wine while it sparkles in the cup.
Wine goes down smoothly. But what does the teacher say it does in the end?

cards.text: "In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper." It's like a cookie that's golden on top, then you flip it over and the bottom is BLACK.

cards.question: The teacher says the drinker's eyes will see ___ things and his mind will utter perversities.
The teacher says the drinker will be like someone sleeping safe in his own bed.

cards.text: Nope, he'll be like one sleeping on the high seas, or lying on the top of a mast. Friend, I wobble on my gold base, and that thing is FLAT, so the TOP of a MAST is a hard no.
Then the teacher lets the drinker talk: "They struck me, but I feel no pain! They beat me, but I did not know it!"

cards.question: The drinker got beaten and didn't even know it. What does he want to do once he wakes up?

answers.text: Find the men who hit him

cards.text: "When can I wake up to search for another drink?" Beat up, and his first plan is round two, but we'll leave it there for now, friend, because the wise aren't done talking yet.

findings.problem: The question says 'Like a robber she lies in wait' but never says who 'she' is. The setup naming the prostitute and the adulteress is on earlier cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: **Always give context in the question.** The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card quotes all six questions of 23:29 and then adds a joke. That makes eight sentences on one card, well past the 1 to 2 sentence limit. Paraphrase the six questions, or quote only a few, so the card stays bite-sized.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: 'We're still listening to the words of the wise' states a fact from outside the passage (Proverbs 22:17), but the card cites only Proverbs 23:15 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.
